title: How Sesame Street teaches kids about emotional well-being, with Rosemarie Truglio, PhD

sentences.en: Sesame Street, the show that has entertained and educated generations of children, is now in its 54th season.
sentences.zh: 《芝麻街》这个给几代儿童带来欢乐和教育的节目，目前正在播出它的第 54 季。

sentences.en: The program has kept pace with the times.
sentences.zh: 这个节目一直与时俱进。

sentences.en: Once primarily known for focusing on ABCs and 123s, Sesame Street has turned its attention over the years to many other topics that touch on children's lives,
sentences.zh: 《芝麻街》过去主要以字母表和 123 数字启蒙而闻名，多年来，它的关注点已经转向了许多触及儿童生活的其他话题，

sentences.en: from grief to race and racism to COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 从悲伤到种族与种族主义，再到 COVID-19。

sentences.en: Last year, Sesame Workshop announced a new focus on the emotional well-being of young children and their families.
sentences.zh: 去年，芝麻工作室宣布了一个新的重点，即关注幼儿及其家庭的情感福祉。

sentences.en: Since then, they've been working with APA and other partners to develop materials to teach young kids about how to understand and manage their feelings.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，他们一直与美国心理协会（APA）及其他合作伙伴合作，开发旨在教导幼儿如何理解和管理自身情绪的材料。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to talk with a psychologist who's worked at Sesame Street for decades about why a focus on young kids' emotional well-being is needed right now.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将与一位在《芝麻街》工作了几十年的心理学家对话，探讨为什么现在如此需要关注幼儿的情感福祉。

sentences.en: How the show translates complicated concepts into stories that young kids can connect with, the research that underpins all the content on Sesame Street,
sentences.zh: 探讨该节目如何将复杂的概念转化为幼儿能够产生共鸣的故事，支撑《芝麻街》所有内容的研究基础，

sentences.en: and what's behind the program's enduring success.
sentences.zh: 以及该节目持久成功的背后原因。

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听美国心理协会的旗舰播客《心理学对话》，该播客探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Rosemary Trulio, a developmental and child psychologist and senior vice president of curriculum and content at Sesame Workshop,
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是罗斯玛丽·特鲁利奥博士，她是一名发展与儿童心理学家，也是芝麻工作室负责课程与内容的资深副总裁，

sentences.en: where she has worked since 1997.
sentences.zh: 她自 1997 年以来一直在这里工作。

sentences.en: She oversees all content and curriculum development for Sesame Street and other shows produced by Sesame Workshop.
sentences.zh: 她监督《芝麻街》以及芝麻工作室制作的其他节目的所有内容和课程开发。

sentences.en: Dr. Trulio has written numerous articles published in child and developmental psychology journals and presented her work at national and international conferences.
sentences.zh: 特鲁利奥博士在儿童与发展心理学期刊上发表了大量文章，并在国家级和国际级会议上发表过研究成果。

sentences.en: She's author of the book, Ready for School, A Parent's Guide to Playful Learning for Children Ages 2 to 5, and co-editor of G is for Growing,
sentences.zh: 她是《准备上学：2至5岁儿童趣味学习家长指南》一书的作者，也是《G代表成长：

sentences.en: 30 Years of Research on Children and Sesame Street.
sentences.zh: 关于儿童与《芝麻街》的 30 年研究》的共同主编。

sentences.en: She has appeared on television and radio programs, including The Today Show, Good Morning America, NPR's Life Kit for Parents, and All Things Considered,
sentences.zh: 她曾亮相电视和广播节目，包括《今日秀》、《早安美国》、美国国家公共电台（NPR）的《家长生活锦囊》和《万物皆知》等，

sentences.en: talking about Sesame Street and offering research-based advice on children and parenting.
sentences.zh: 畅谈《芝麻街》，并就儿童和育儿问题提供基于研究的建议。

sentences.en: Dr. Trulio, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 特鲁利奥博士，非常感谢您今天能来做客。

sentences.en: Oh, thank you, Kim.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢你，金。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure to be talking with you today.
sentences.zh: 很高兴今天能与你交谈。

sentences.en: I mentioned in the intro that Sesame Workshop announced a multi-year commitment to focusing on children's emotional well-being last year.
sentences.zh: 我在开场白中提到，芝麻工作室去年宣布了一项为期多年的承诺，专注于儿童的情感福祉。

sentences.en: Why did you decide that this was such an important topic to focus on right now?
sentences.zh: 为什么你们决定这是一个现在如此重要的关注话题？

sentences.en: It's a very important topic because we have a global mental health crisis.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重要的课题，因为我们正面临全球心理健康危机。

sentences.en: And Sesame, from its inception,
sentences.zh: 而《芝麻街》自创立以来，

sentences.en: has always been there to help children and the caregivers and adults in their lives to help them build what we call these foundational skills to get them ready for school and to get them ready for life.
sentences.zh: 一直都在那里，帮助儿童以及他们生活中的照料者和成年人，帮助他们培养我们所说的这些基础技能，为他们做好上学的准备，并为他们的生活做好准备。

sentences.en: So, Sesame Street is driven by what we call a whole-child curriculum.
sentences.zh: 因此，《芝麻街》是由我们所谓的“全人儿童课程”驱动的。

sentences.en: So, we're dealing with all aspects of child development.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们在处理儿童发展的各个方面。

sentences.en: Their academic skills, their social-emotional skills, their health needs.
sentences.zh: 他们的学业技能、社交情感技能、健康需求。

sentences.en: And we're very much in tune to what is going on in terms of the latest research, the best practices, as well as what's going on in our society.
sentences.zh: 我们非常关注最新研究、最佳实践以及我们社会中正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: So, when it was announced that there's a global health crisis, which was there before the pandemic but just got exacerbated with the pandemic, that we decided,
sentences.zh: 因此，当宣布存在全球健康危机时——这在疫情之前就已存在，但在疫情期间进一步加剧——我们决定，

sentences.en: because we always have a curriculum focus every year,
sentences.zh: 因为我们每年都有一个课程重点，

sentences.en: and we decided that we can make a difference and provide foundational information to help build the foundation of what we're calling emotional well-being.
sentences.zh: 我们决定我们可以发挥作用，提供基础信息，为我们称之为情感福祉的东西奠定基础。

sentences.en: How do you teach young children about a complicated topic like emotional well-being?
sentences.zh: 你如何向幼儿教授像情感福祉这样复杂的概念？

sentences.en: How is it different from developing content for older children or adults?
sentences.zh: 这与为较大儿童或成年人开发内容有什么不同？

sentences.en: Well, we have to keep in mind that we're talking to an audience that ranges from ages 2 to age 5, and we need to make sure that the content is meaningful and relevant to them,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们必须记住，我们的受众年龄在 2 岁到 5 岁之间，我们需要确保内容对他们来说是有意义且相关的，

sentences.en: as well as engaging for them.
sentences.zh: 同时也必须是引人入胜的。

sentences.en: Because we know that those are critical factors to keep children paying attention to the messages, but also when they're engaged with content, it helps with the comprehension.
sentences.zh: 因为我们知道，这些是让儿童保持对信息注意力К关键因素，而且当他们投入到内容中时，也有助于理解。

sentences.en: So, we make sure that our goals are developmentally appropriate, but we never, ever talk down to children.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们确保我们的目标符合发展阶段，但我们绝不会用居高临下的态度对儿童说话。

sentences.en: So, we want to make sure that the stories have meaning in their lives, and we give them what we call the vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们要确保故事在他们的生活中具有意义，并且我们赋予他们所谓的词汇。

sentences.en: So, we focused a lot on the vocabulary for emotional awareness, because we know with really young children, they have a range of big feelings,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们在情感认知的词汇上下了很大功夫，因为我们知道对于极小的儿童来说，他们会有各种各样强烈的情感，

sentences.en: but they don't have the words to express these feelings.
sentences.zh: 但他们没有表达这些情感的词汇。

sentences.en: And the adults in their lives, and the adults in their lives also have to remind them of the nuances in terms of the vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 他们生活中的成年人，以及他们生活中的成年人也必须提醒他们在词汇上的细微差别。

sentences.en: So, angry versus frustrated versus disappointed, and not be afraid to use these big words, but to define them in the moment of the scenario that they're feeling.
sentences.zh: 比如生气与沮丧与失望的区别，不要害怕使用这些大词，而要在他们感受到这种情绪的具体场景中去定义它们。

sentences.en: So, they have an understanding of the meaningfulness of that word.
sentences.zh: 这样，他们就能理解这个词的意义。

sentences.en: And when you're dealing with audiovisual content, to make sure that there's a term that we use is say and see.
sentences.zh: 当你在处理视听内容时，要确保有一个我们称之为“说与看”的原则。

sentences.en: Make sure that the visuals are in tune to what they're hearing.
sentences.zh: 确保视觉效果与他们所听到的一致。

sentences.en: And gestures.
sentences.zh: 还有手势。

sentences.en: Gestures are really important in terms of comprehension.
sentences.zh: 手势对于理解非常重要。

sentences.en: So, as you could hear me saying, we do a lot of research.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如你听到我所说的，我们做了大量的研究。

sentences.en: We are culling from the academic research that's coming from the learning sciences, and we also engage in our own what we call formative research.
sentences.zh: 我们从学习科学的学术研究中汲取营养，同时我们也开展我们所谓的形成性研究。

sentences.en: Because even though I have a doctorate in developmental psychology, I'm constantly learning from children.
sentences.zh: 因为尽管我拥有发展心理学博士学位，但我一直在向儿童学习。

sentences.en: They're the real experts.
sentences.zh: 他们才是真正的专家。

sentences.en: I may think this is going to work, but then we show children, and they're telling us what's working for them.
sentences.zh: 我可能认为这会行之有效，但当我们向儿童展示时，他们会告诉我们什么对他们管用。

sentences.en: One of your newest videos is about feelings helpers.
sentences.zh: 你们最新的视频之一是关于情绪助手的。

sentences.en: It's a way of introducing children to the idea of therapy and mental health professionals.
sentences.zh: 这是向儿童介绍治疗和心理健康专业人员概念的一种方式。

sentences.en: I'm a special helper, too.
sentences.zh: 我也是一个特殊的助手。

sentences.en: Sophia is really?
sentences.zh: 索菲亚，真的吗？

sentences.en: My costume.
sentences.zh: 我的戏服。

sentences.en: This is my costume.
sentences.zh: 这是我的戏服。

sentences.en: This is what I wear when I do my job.
sentences.zh: 这就是我工作时穿的衣服。

sentences.en: I am a therapist, a counselor.
sentences.zh: 我是一名治疗师，一名心理咨询师。

sentences.en: I'm a feelings helper.
sentences.zh: 我是一个情绪助手。

sentences.en: Can you tell us about that?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我们讲讲这个吗？

sentences.en: How did you come up with the idea of feelings helpers?
sentences.zh: 你们是怎么想出“情绪助手”这个主意的？

sentences.en: I'm really glad you asked me that question.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你问我这个问题。

sentences.en: When we start a new initiative for a new season of content, both show content and also we have a tremendous amount of content, free resources on our website.
sentences.zh: 当我们为一个新的内容季启动新项目时，既包括节目内容，而且我们在网站上也有大量的内容和免费资源。

sentences.en: So, sesamestreet.org in this particular initiative, it's backslash mental health.
sentences.zh: 因此，sesamestreet.org 在这个特定项目中的网址是斜杠 mental health（心理健康）。

sentences.en: And these resources are there for parents and caregivers and educators to use.
sentences.zh: 这些资源可供家长、照料者和教育工作者使用。

sentences.en: But we always start with what we call an advisory curriculum seminar.
sentences.zh: 但我们总是从我们所谓的咨询课程研讨会开始。

sentences.en: And that's where we bring in the experts to help us.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们请来专家来帮助我们的地方。

sentences.en: Help us figure out what goals should we focus on and then how to move forward in terms of content creation.
sentences.zh: 帮助我们弄清楚我们应该关注哪些目标，然后如何在内容创作方面推进。

sentences.en: So, as I said, we have a mental health crisis.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我们面临着心理健康危机。

sentences.en: And for the most part, we're just focusing on emotional well-being, which are these foundational skills.
sentences.zh: 在很大程度上，我们只是专注于情感福祉，也就是这些基础技能。

sentences.en: So, that is emotional awareness, social connections, mind-body connections, and compassionate mindset.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，情感认知、社会联系、身心连接和同理心思维。

sentences.en: We could talk about these four domains later.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后可以讨论这四个领域。

sentences.en: But on the website,
sentences.zh: 但在网站上，

sentences.en: we also wanted to bring attention to destigmatize mental health in terms of there are times in children's lives that these basic foundational skills aren't enough.
sentences.zh: 我们还想引起人们对消除心理健康污名化的关注，因为在儿童的生活中，有时这些基本的基础技能是不够的。

sentences.en: That their big feelings are impeding with their everyday moments or things that they want to do, such as anxiety, right?
sentences.zh: 他们强烈的情感正在妨碍他们的日常生活或他们想要做的事情，比如焦虑，对吧？

sentences.en: We want parents and caregivers and educators to know that it is okay to then get additional help.
sentences.zh: 我们希望家长、照料者和教育工作者知道，去寻求额外的帮助是没有问题的。

sentences.en: Now, children are used to going to the pediatrician.
sentences.zh: 现在，儿童习惯去看儿科医生。

sentences.en: They go to the doctor.
sentences.zh: 他们去看医生。

sentences.en: But what do you call the person who is helping them with their big feelings?
sentences.zh: 但是，你怎么称呼那个帮助他们应对强烈情感的人呢？

sentences.en: And one of the advisors said, you know, we don't want to call them therapists or counselors.
sentences.zh: 其中一位顾问说，你知道，我们不想称他们为治疗师或咨询师。

sentences.en: What does that mean for a child?
sentences.zh: 这对一个孩子意味着什么？

sentences.en: So, we're going to call them feelings helpers.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们要称他们为情绪助手。

sentences.en: These are special people who help us have a better understanding of what the emotions that are overwhelming and taking over.
sentences.zh: 这些人是特殊的人，能帮助我们更好地理解那些压倒我们、接管我们的情绪到底是什么。

sentences.en: More importantly, what are the strategies to help be with those big feelings when they come up?
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，当这些强烈情感出现时，有哪些策略可以帮助我们与之相处。

sentences.en: And it's really important sometimes to talk to someone who is skilled in helping them.
sentences.zh: 有时候，与一个擅长帮助他们的人交谈真的非常重要。

sentences.en: And they are your counselors, your mental health professionals.
sentences.zh: 他们就是你的咨询师，你的心理健康专业人士。

sentences.en: But for children, they're feelings helpers.
sentences.zh: 但对于儿童来说，他们是情绪助手。

sentences.en: Can you tell us a little bit more about your role at Sesame Workshop?
sentences.zh: 你能多讲讲你在芝麻工作室扮演的角色吗？

sentences.en: I mean, what do you do as the vice president of curriculum and content?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，作为课程与内容副总裁，你具体做些什么？

sentences.en: Are you convening these groups or reviewing the science or a little of everything?
sentences.zh: 你是召集这些小组、审查科学研究，还是各种事情都做一点？

sentences.en: Okay, so, as the senior vice president for curriculum and content, it's my responsibility to help our organization figure out what are we going to focus on.
sentences.zh: 好的，那么，作为课程与内容的资深副总裁，我的职责是帮助我们的组织弄清楚我们要关注什么。

sentences.en: You know, so, yes, we are a school readiness.
sentences.zh: 你知道，是的，我们是一个学校准备项目。

sentences.en: We're all based on a school readiness curriculum.
sentences.zh: 我们全都基于学校准备课程。

sentences.en: But then sometimes we have to hone in and put a spotlight on what's going on and being in tune to what's going on in our society.
sentences.zh: 但有时我们必须聚焦并将聚光灯投向正在发生的事情，并与我们社会中正在发生的事情保持一致。

sentences.en: So, when we decided that we were going to focus on emotional well-being, I then have a convening.
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们决定专注于情感福祉时，我随后会组织一次会议。

sentences.en: And I have a colleague who's also a senior vice president who oversees our U.S.
sentences.zh: 我有一位同事，他也是一位资深副总裁，负责监督我们的美国

sentences.en: social impact work.
sentences.zh: 社会影响力工作。

sentences.en: And that's the work that you're going to find on the website.
sentences.zh: 这就是你将在网站上看到的工作。

sentences.en: So, sesamestreet.org backslash mental health.
sentences.zh: 所以，sesamestreet.org 斜杠 mental health。

sentences.en: And so, I help her with her convening.
sentences.zh: 因此，我协助她的会议。

sentences.en: She helps me with my convening because they're very different audiences.
sentences.zh: 她协助我的会议，因为他们的受众非常不同。

sentences.en: So, for me, my responsibility is for what we call mass media.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，我的职责是针对我们所说的大众媒体。

sentences.en: So, helping the content creators who are writing for the show, who are writing for digital, who are overseeing our publishing department, our licensing department.
sentences.zh: 因此，帮助为节目写作、为数字平台写作的内容创作者，以及监督我们的出版部门、我们的授权部门。

sentences.en: So, messages that are going out there that are directed to children.
sentences.zh: 所以，发布给儿童的那些信息。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 所以，

sentences.en: child-facing messages with the hope that the adults are going to be co-engaged with them through reading a book or watching the show or playing a digital game or listening to a podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 面向儿童的信息，希望成年人能够通过阅读一本书、观看节目、玩数字游戏或听播客与他们共同参与进来。

sentences.en: My colleague, Dr. Jeanette Bettencourt, her focus is the website.
sentences.zh: 我的同事珍妮特·贝滕库尔特博士（Dr. Jeanette Bettencourt），她的重点是网站。

sentences.en: And so, that's more adult-facing with the understanding that for some content, you want to be able to – an adult may want to bring the child and watch and co-engage in the video.
sentences.zh: 因此，这更多是面向成人的，其理解是对于某些内容，你希望能够——成年人可能希望带上孩子一起观看并共同参与视频。

sentences.en: And there's lots of child-facing content, you know, printables and storybooks that are child-facing.
sentences.zh: 而且有很多面向儿童的内容，你知道的，可打印材料和面向儿童的故事书。

sentences.en: But then there's also adult-directed information for the adults in their lives to help them with some of these learning goals.
sentences.zh: 但也有针对他们生活中的成年人的信息，以帮助他们实现其中一些学习目标。

sentences.en: Now, I also mentioned in the intro that you were the co-editor of G is for Growing, 30 years of research on children and Sesame Street.
sentences.zh: 现在，我在开场白中还提到你是《G代表成长：关于儿童与《芝麻街》的 30 年研究》的共同主编。

sentences.en: And I'm going to guess that a lot of our listeners have no idea that there's been so much research into Sesame Street and its viewers.
sentences.zh: 我猜我们的很多听众根本不知道原来有这么多的研究是针对《芝麻街》及其观众的。

sentences.en: And your book was really the first time that this research was examined holistically.
sentences.zh: 而你的书确实是第一次对这些研究进行整体审视。

sentences.en: And I know this was a weighty and serious tome, but could you summarize some of the key findings?
sentences.zh: 我知道这是一部厚重严肃的大部头，你能总结一下其中的一些关键发现吗？

sentences.en: Oh, well, that's great.
sentences.zh: 哦，好的，那太棒了。

sentences.en: And so, that book – that brings us up to, you know, season one to season 29.
sentences.zh: 所以，那本书——这把我们带到了，你知道的，从第一季到第 29 季。

sentences.en: And I want to mention another book that was co-edited by colleagues called The Sesame Effect.
sentences.zh: 我想提另一本书，是由同事共同主编的，叫做《芝麻效应》。

sentences.en: And that book also shows all of the research on our international productions because we are a global educational media company.
sentences.zh: 那本书还展示了关于我们国际制作的所有研究，因为我们是一家全球教育媒体公司。

sentences.en: And in The Sesame Effect, there is a chapter that starts with season 30's educational impact to about season 50.
sentences.zh: 在《芝麻效应》中，有一章从第 30 季的教育影响一直写到大约第 50 季。

sentences.en: So, we're probably the best-kept secret.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们可能是保守得最好的秘密。

sentences.en: What I mean by that is that a lot of people don't realize the amount of learning science that goes into the creation of our content, the formative research.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很多人并没有意识到有多少学习科学被投入到我们内容的创作中，以及形成性研究。

sentences.en: So, as I said earlier, that for us, children are the best experts.
sentences.zh: 因此，正如我刚才所说，对我们而言，儿童是最好的专家。

sentences.en: So, we want to make sure for child-facing content that we're out there talking to, showing, and talking to children.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们要确保对于面向儿童的内容，我们要走出去与儿童交谈、向他们展示并与他们交谈。

sentences.en: On the website content, we want to make sure that the content works for caregivers and educators.
sentences.zh: 对于网站内容，我们要确保内容对照料者和教育工作者管用。

sentences.en: So, formative research is being done with those target audiences.
sentences.zh: 因此，形成性研究是在这些目标受众中进行的。

sentences.en: This is a key component of Sesame Workshop's content creation.
sentences.zh: 这是芝麻工作室内容创作的关键组成部分。

sentences.en: But it doesn't stop there, right?
sentences.zh: 但这并没有结束，对吧？

sentences.en: So, we want to make sure the inputs are great for putting our best foot forward in terms of getting an educational impact.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们要确保输入很棒，以便在获得教育影响力方面迈出最好的一步。

sentences.en: But then we've got to do the summit of research, the impact research.
sentences.zh: 但接着我们必须做总结性研究，也就是影响力研究。

sentences.en: And so, both books are summaries of the educational impact that we've had, both in the areas of academic skills, so literacy and language development, math and science,
sentences.zh: 因此，这两本书都是我们所获得的教育影响的总结，无论是在学术技能领域，即读写能力和语言发展、数学和科学，

sentences.en: social-emotional skills and development, and health.
sentences.zh: 还是社交情感技能与发展，以及健康。

sentences.en: There's a lot of emphasis placed on our physical health.
sentences.zh: 我们的身体健康受到了很大的重视。

sentences.en: And so, both books show you the breadth of the content that we're addressing, but most importantly, the educational impact that we're having.
sentences.zh: 因此，这两本书向你展示了我们正在解决的内容的广度，但最重要的是，展示了我们正在产生的教育影响。

sentences.en: And most recently, which I believe has been released, is that we have done a lot of work in the Middle East with a new co-production called Aham Simpson.
sentences.zh: 最近，我相信已经发布的是，我们在中东做了大量工作，推出了一个名为《Aham Simpson》的新联合制作项目。

sentences.en: And that is to focus on the Syrian refugee crisis.
sentences.zh: 这是为了关注叙利亚难民危机。

sentences.en: So, and that work really did focus a lot on emotional well-being.
sentences.zh: 所以，这项工作确实非常关注情感福祉。

sentences.en: So, looking at this research over such a long period of time, have you found that kids who grew up on Sesame Street were better in school, grew up healthier, were better adjusted,
sentences.zh: 因此，纵观这么长时间的研究，你是否发现从小看《芝麻街》长大的孩子在学校表现更好、成长得更健康、适应能力更好，

sentences.en: all of those things that you might want to be able to measure?
sentences.zh: 所有你可能想要测量的事情？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, there were a couple of seminal pieces of research that were longitudinal research studies, which is really hard to do now.
sentences.zh: 所以，有几项开创性的研究是纵向研究，现在这真的很难做到。

sentences.en: These were conducted in the early 90s, but it showed that children who watched Sesame Street during the preschool years did significantly better in high school.
sentences.zh: 这些是在 90 年代初进行的，但它表明，在学龄前观看《芝麻街》的儿童在高中时的表现明显更好。

sentences.en: They were able to recontact those children, children living in Springfield, Massachusetts and Topeka, Kansas.
sentences.zh: 他们能够重新联系到那些儿童，即生活在马萨诸塞州斯普林菲尔德和堪萨斯州托皮卡的儿童。

sentences.en: So, that's called the recontact study, which is in the G's for Growing, summarizing the G's for Growing book.
sentences.zh: 所以，这被称为重新联系研究，它被收录在《G代表成长》一书中，总结在《G代表成长》一书中。

sentences.en: What we found with Aham Simpson recently is that because as we were doing this research, there was a pandemic,
sentences.zh: 我们最近在《Aham Simpson》中发现的是，因为在我们做这项研究时，发生了疫情，

sentences.en: and so some of the work had to be moved to digital through a digital device.
sentences.zh: 因此部分工作不得不通过数字设备转移到线上。

sentences.en: And they found that the content that was consumed over a, I don't know, maybe a six or seven-week period, was the learning impact was the equivalent of going to school,
sentences.zh: 他们发现，在大概六、七周的时间里所消费的内容，其学习效果相当于去学校

sentences.en: a physical building, for a whole year.
sentences.zh: 也就是一所实体学校，整整读了一年。

sentences.en: So, just think about the power of that, to deliver our content through a digital device, reaching children.
sentences.zh: 所以，试想一下这种力量，通过数字设备将我们的内容传递给孩子们。

sentences.en: This is true, you know, for around the world in terms of trying to get to remote areas where children may not be able to get to preschool.
sentences.zh: 这确实如此，你知道，在世界各地都是这样，因为我们试图触及那些孩子们可能无法去幼儿园的偏远地区。

sentences.en: So, we're pretty, we're very pleased by the results of that study, and it shows the power of our educational content.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们对这项研究的结果感到非常满意，这展示了我们教育内容的力量。

sentences.en: How do you identify the needs in kids so that you can tailor the right messages at the right time?
sentences.zh: 你们是如何识别孩子们的需求，以便在合适的时间量身定制合适的信息的？

sentences.en: Well, we're very much connected to the academic community.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们与学术界紧密相连。

sentences.en: So, I'll give you an example of that, you know, in the early 2000s when all of the focus was on brain development.
sentences.zh: 所以我举个例子，你知道，在2000年代初，所有的焦点都在大脑发育上。

sentences.en: You know, we learned a lot as developmental psychologists.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，作为发展心理学家，我们学到了很多。

sentences.en: And so, there was a lot of talk about self-regulation and executive function skills.
sentences.zh: 当时有很多关于自我调节和执行功能技能的讨论。

sentences.en: Well, that was never a part of our school readiness curriculum, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这从来都不是我们入学准备课程的一部分，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, we've learned from the learning sciences that, wow, you know, we need to start focusing more on those process skills.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们从学习科学中了解到，哇，你知道的，我们需要开始更多地关注这些过程技能。

sentences.en: How do children learn content, right?
sentences.zh: 孩子们是如何学习内容的，对吧？

sentences.en: We've been focusing on the content skills.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在关注内容技能。

sentences.en: You know, as you said, letters and numbers and you're, you know, and identifying feelings and maybe talk about healthy foods and the importance of exercise.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，正如你所说，字母和数字，还有，你知道的，识别情绪，也许谈谈健康食品和锻炼的重要性。

sentences.en: But what are those skills that are the true school readiness skills?
sentences.zh: 但究竟什么是真正的入学准备技能？

sentences.en: And we've learned through the research that it is those executive function skills, the ability to pay attention, the ability to focus your attention,
sentences.zh: 我们通过研究了解到，正是那些执行功能技能，即保持注意力的能力，专注注意力的能力，

sentences.en: but also be able to shift your attention and have flexible thinking.
sentences.zh: 还要能够转移注意力并具备灵活的思维。

sentences.en: The ability to control your emotions that might be interfering with your ability to pay attention.
sentences.zh: 控制那些可能会妨碍你专注的情绪的能力。

sentences.en: So, we revised our whole child curriculum based on those research findings and put those executive functions skills at the core of academic learning, social-emotional learning,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们根据这些研究结果修订了全人教育课程，将这些执行功能技能置于学术学习、社交情感学习的核心，

sentences.en: and health, health behaviors.
sentences.zh: 还有健康、健康行为。

sentences.en: Another example is when there was all this focus on STEM education.
sentences.zh: 另一个例子是当全社会都聚焦于STEM教育时。

sentences.en: And a lot of people said, well, Sesame Street can't focus on STEM.
sentences.zh: 许多人说，好吧，《芝麻街》不能专注于STEM。

sentences.en: You know, you're, you know, you're, you're talking to, you know, little kids, little kids.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你，你知道的，你，你在和，你知道的，小孩子们对话，小孩子们。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's, that's, that's in, you know, high school, maybe, maybe middle school.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，那是，那是，那是，你知道的，高中生，也许是初中生该学的。

sentences.en: And was like, no, no, no, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 当时我们的反应是，不，不，不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: Preschoolers are natural STEMists.
sentences.zh: 学龄前儿童天生就是STEM实践者。

sentences.en: They're scientists, they're technologists, they're engineers, and they're mathematicians.
sentences.zh: 他们是科学家、技术人员、工程师和数学家。

sentences.en: And so, once again, we focused on those process skills, you know, the power of investigation, power of observation, the power of analyzing,
sentences.zh: 所以，再次强调，我们专注于这些过程技能，你知道的，探索的力量、观察的力量、分析的力量，

sentences.en: because they're doing that all the time as they're trying to figure out the world around them.
sentences.zh: 因为他们在试图理解周围世界时一直在这样做。

sentences.en: And so, we created a STEM curriculum, and we have our characters solving everyday problems using these process skills.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们创建了一个STEM课程，让我们的角色运用这些过程技能来解决日常生活中的问题。

sentences.en: And then at the, at the end of the solving of the problem, they're learning a science fact, or a math fact, or an engineering fact.
sentences.zh: 然后在问题解决的最后，他们学到了一个科学事实、数学事实或工程学事实。

sentences.en: So, those are two examples.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是两个例子。

sentences.en: It sounds like the researchers are learning as much from the kids as the kids are learning from watching the shows.
sentences.zh: 听起来研究人员从孩子们身上学到的东西，和孩子们看节目学到的一样多。

sentences.en: Is that true?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Is that true?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And I think that's why I've been here for multiple decades, because I'm constantly learning.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是我在这里待了几十年的原因，因为我在不断地学习。

sentences.en: So, I have to ask you about Elmo's viral moment on social media a few months ago.
sentences.zh: 所以我不得不问你关于几个月前埃尔莫在社交媒体上引发轰动的事。

sentences.en: Elmo posted a question on X, formerly Twitter.
sentences.zh: 埃尔莫在X（前身为Twitter）上发了一个问题。

sentences.en: He said, Elmo is just checking in.
sentences.zh: 他说，埃尔莫只是来问候一下。

sentences.en: How is everybody doing?
sentences.zh: 大家最近都怎么样？

sentences.en: And he was inundated with replies about people's mental and emotional states, and some people even called it trauma dumping.
sentences.zh: 结果他收到了大量关于人们心理和情感状态的回复，甚至有人称之为“倾倒创伤”。

sentences.en: Were you and the other people at Sesame Street surprised by this moment?
sentences.zh: 你和《芝麻街》的其他工作人员对这一刻感到惊讶吗？

sentences.en: We were surprised by the large number of people writing in.
sentences.zh: 我们对有如此多的人写信回复感到惊讶。

sentences.en: That was surprising, but not 100% surprised, because we know that we are dealing with a mental health crisis.
sentences.zh: 这确实令人惊讶，但也不是百分之百意外，因为我们知道我们正处于心理健康危机之中。

sentences.en: And not surprised by adults' connection with our characters.
sentences.zh: 而且对于成年人与我们的角色之间的联系，我们并不感到意外。

sentences.en: And I think that is the power of our Sesame Street brand, is that multiple generations now have grown up on Sesame Street.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是我们《芝麻街》品牌的力量所在，那就是好几代人都是看着《芝麻街》长大的。

sentences.en: And these characters have meaning in our lives.
sentences.zh: 这些角色在我们的生活中具有特殊意义。

sentences.en: And so, also learning from the developmental psychology research, is that when you're a child and you are connected to a character,
sentences.zh: 因此，从发展心理学研究中我们也了解到，当你还是个孩子并且与某个角色建立连接时，

sentences.en: you develop what we call a power social relationship.
sentences.zh: 你就会培养出我们所谓的拟社会关系。

sentences.en: Elmo is talking to me.
sentences.zh: 埃尔莫在跟我说话。

sentences.en: Elmo is my friend.
sentences.zh: 埃尔莫是我的朋友。

sentences.en: I can talk to Elmo.
sentences.zh: 我可以和埃尔莫说话。

sentences.en: Elmo cares about me, and Elmo loves me.
sentences.zh: 埃尔莫关心我，埃尔莫爱我。

sentences.en: So, think about the people who are on X and social media.
sentences.zh: 所以，想想那些在X和社交媒体上的人。

sentences.en: They're adults, but they have these emotional connections to Elmo.
sentences.zh: 他们是成年人，但他们对埃尔莫有着这些情感连接。

sentences.en: And by Elmo reaching out, how are you doing?
sentences.zh: 随着埃尔莫主动问候“你们最近怎么样？”，

sentences.en: They then revealed how they were doing.
sentences.zh: 他们便倾诉了自己最近的现状。

sentences.en: And what was wonderful is that we also, because that was a year into our initiative, we now had resources to say, go to SesameStreet.org.
sentences.zh: 而美妙的是，由于这也是我们开展该计划满一年之际，我们现在有了相应的资源可以告诉大家：访问SesameStreet.org。

sentences.en: We are there for you.
sentences.zh: 我们在那里为你守候。

sentences.en: You are not alone.
sentences.zh: 你并不孤单。

sentences.en: We are here for you, and we will always be here for you.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里支持你，而且永远都会在这里支持你。

sentences.en: I have to ask a question about the early days of Sesame Street, because I grew up when educational TV was just beginning, and it was awful.
sentences.zh: 我得问一个关于《芝麻街》早期的问题，因为我成长于教育电视刚刚起步的年代，当时那个太糟糕了。

sentences.en: It was like a teacher standing in a classroom, and the only difference was you were watching on a screen instead of in reality.
sentences.zh: 就像一个老师站在教室里，唯一的区别是你看着屏幕而不是在现实中。

sentences.en: And it was in black and white.
sentences.zh: 而且还是黑白的。

sentences.en: I'm really dating myself here.
sentences.zh: 我这可真是在暴露年龄了。

sentences.en: But then in 1969, Sesame Street came on television, and it was completely revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 但后来在1969年，《芝麻街》登上了电视荧屏，这完全是一场革命。

sentences.en: Kids loved it, and they learned things.
sentences.zh: 孩子们喜欢它，并且学到了东西。

sentences.en: What was different about Sesame Street, and why do you think it's persisted for all these decades?
sentences.zh: $芝麻街$有何不同之处，你认为它为什么能历经数十年而不衰？

sentences.en: A tremendous amount of research went into the design and the making of Sesame Street.
sentences.zh: $芝麻街$的设计和制作投入了大量的研究。

sentences.en: First, let's start with our co-founder, Joan Ganzconi, who knew that, you know, at the time, she was a documentary producer and focused on, you know,
sentences.zh: 首先，让我们从我们的联合创始人琼·甘兹·库尼（Joan Ganz Cooney）开始，她当时知道，作为一个纪录片制作人，她专注于，你知道的，

sentences.en: what's going on in terms of the educational needs of children.
sentences.zh: 孩子们在教育需求方面正在发生什么。

sentences.en: She wanted to make sure that by creating a television show that we could reach children, in particular children who didn't have access to preschool education,
sentences.zh: 她希望通过制作一档电视节目来接触儿童，特别是那些无法接受学前教育的儿童，

sentences.en: so the disadvantaged children, and to make sure that giving them an even start, right, to get them ready for school.
sentences.zh: 也就是弱势儿童，并确保给他们一个平等的起跑线，对吧，让他们为上学做好准备。

sentences.en: But because she came from television as a producer, she noticed that young children watching TV, vast wasteland, were able to recite jingles from commercials.
sentences.zh: 但由于她作为制片人出身电视行业，她注意到幼儿在看电视时——那片“浩瀚的荒漠”——却能背出商业广告里的短歌谣。

sentences.en: And she's like, wow, if we could teach them commercial jingles, think about how we could teach them school readiness skills in little pieces of television.
sentences.zh: 她说，哇，如果我们能教他们广告歌谣，想想看，我们怎么能通过一小段一小段的电视节目来教他们入学准备技能呢。

sentences.en: So that was her premise, but she had no idea if this was going to work, and so she got a grant to say, all right, this is an experiment.
sentences.zh: $这就是她的前提，但她不知道这是否行得通，于是她申请了一笔资助，说，好吧，这是一场实验。

sentences.en: No one's ever tried this.
sentences.zh: 从来没有人尝试过这个。

sentences.en: Give it a shot.
sentences.zh: 试一试吧。

sentences.en: And so she's the one who created this model.
sentences.zh: $所以她是创建这个模式的人。

sentences.en: We got to think out of the box, as you said, we just can't have a classroom that is just being filmed.
sentences.zh: $我们必须跳出框架思考，正如你所说，我们不能只拍摄一个教室。

sentences.en: We got to get their attention, all right, just like a commercial gets their attention.
sentences.zh: $我们必须抓住他们的注意力，好吧，就像商业广告抓住他们的注意力一样。

sentences.en: So she assembled the developmental psychologist, she assembled the early childhood educators who know how to create curriculum, and she brought in Jim Henson, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，她集结了发展心理学家，集结了懂得如何创建课程的幼儿教育工作者，还请来了吉姆·汉森（Jim Henson），对吧？

sentences.en: She wanted to make sure that the street was going to be grounded in reality.
sentences.zh: $她想确保这条街道能够扎根于现实。

sentences.en: It's a real street.
sentences.zh: $这是一条真实的街道。

sentences.en: We're going to have a human cast, a diverse and inclusive human caSt.
sentences.zh: $我们将拥有一套人类演员班底，一个多元化且包容的人类演员阵容。

sentences.en: She wants to make sure that she's reaching all children.
sentences.zh: $她希望确保自己能够接触到所有的孩子。

sentences.en: But she also wanted to bring in that fantasy, and that's where Jim and his characters came about, right?
sentences.zh: 但她也想引入那种幻想元素，这就是吉姆和他的角色们诞生的地方，对吧？

sentences.en: So Sesame Street is grounded in reality, which is really important for us to hold on to.
sentences.zh: $所以《芝麻街》立足于现实，这对于我们坚持下去非常重要。

sentences.en: It remains a live-action show, and because it's live-action, we can always create content to meet the current needs of children.
sentences.zh: $它依然是一个真人实景节目，正因为它是真人实景，我们才能随时创作内容以满足孩子们当前的需求。

sentences.en: So we're constantly evolving and very dynamic.
sentences.zh: 所以我们一直在不断演变，非常具有活力。

sentences.en: So we're always making show changes.
sentences.zh: $因此我们一直在对节目进行调整。

sentences.en: And so get back to your question, it's like, why are we surviving?
sentences.zh: 回到你的问题，就像是，为什么我们能生存下来？

sentences.en: Because the show that we created in 1969 is not the show that's currently airing in 2024, season 54, because we're creating a show that meets the needs of today's children.
sentences.zh: 因为我们在1969年创作的节目并不是2024年正在播出的第五十四季节目，因为我们正在创作一档满足当今儿童需求的节目。

sentences.en: And I think that's what makes us unique and special.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是让我们独特和特殊的地方。

sentences.en: Have kids' needs changed over time?
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，孩子们的需求变了吗？

sentences.en: I mean, some things are very fundamental and must be the same from generation to generation.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有些东西是非常基础的，代代相传必须保持一致。

sentences.en: But what's new with today's kids?
sentences.zh: 但如今的孩子们有什么新鲜的需求？

sentences.en: Well, I think there are different things going on in today's world.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为当今世界正在发生各种不同的事情。

sentences.en: I think really focusing on emotional well-being is something that's very important.
sentences.zh: 我认为真正专注于情感健康是非常重要的一点。

sentences.en: We know that these executive function skills, which children struggle with, we know that these are learned skills.
sentences.zh: 我们知道这些孩子们感到吃力的执行功能技能，其实是可以通过后天学习掌握的技能。

sentences.en: So that was a big change in our curriculum.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们课程中的一大改变。

sentences.en: Focus on physical health.
sentences.zh: 关注身体健康。

sentences.en: Children don't understand what it means to be healthy.
sentences.zh: 孩子们并不理解保持健康意味着什么。

sentences.en: That means I'm not sick, right?
sentences.zh: 那意味着我没有生病，对吧？

sentences.en: But how do you give them these what we call healthy habits for life?
sentences.zh: 但如何赋予他们我们所谓的“终身健康习惯”呢？

sentences.en: And in terms of academic skills, we're constantly learning about what are best practices.
sentences.zh: 在学术技能方面，我们一直在了解什么是最佳实践。

sentences.en: So, for instance, there was a lot of emphasis placed on vocabulary development, right?
sentences.zh: 例如，过去非常强调词汇量的发展，对吧？

sentences.en: Remember the $30 million, not $30 million word gap.
sentences.zh: 还记得那个3000万词汇差距的说法吗？

sentences.en: So, we learned a lot about that, that it's, you know, not just showing the letter, what the letter sounds like, so that's phonemic awareness, but also building vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 所以我们从中学到了很多，这不仅是展示字母、弄清楚字母的发音——也就是音素意识，还要建立词汇量。

sentences.en: And that was an important lesson to us, too, when we were focusing on math, that children, while they may have an understanding of math concepts,
sentences.zh: 这对我们也是一个重要教训，当我们专注于数学时，我们发现孩子们虽然可能对数学概念有所理解，

sentences.en: they may not have the math language.
sentences.zh: 但他们可能缺乏相应的数学语言。

sentences.en: And so, there was a big focus on math literacy, and that came out of the academic research.
sentences.zh: 因此，当时非常重视数学素养，这正是学术研究所得出的成果。

sentences.en: In addition to the show itself, Sesame Workshop has a lot of other avenues to get resources out to caregivers and children.
sentences.zh: 除了节目本身，《芝麻街工作室》还有许多其他途径将资源送达照料者和儿童手中。

sentences.en: Can you tell our listeners some more about the other resources that are available to help kids learn about emotional well-being?
sentences.zh: 你能向我们的听众详细介绍一下，还有哪些可用的资源来帮助孩子们了解情感健康吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, as I mentioned on our website, sesamestreet.org backslash mental health, there's a lot of information that we released and are continuing to release.
sentences.zh: 正如我提到的，在我们的网站 sesamestreet.org/mentalhealth 上，我们发布了大量信息，并且还将继续发布。

sentences.en: And so, there will be new information coming up in early May.
sentences.zh: $因此，在五月初将会有新的信息推出。

sentences.en: So, definitely check back.
sentences.zh: 所以，一定要记得回来查看。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think by the time we post this, some of that should be up.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想在我们发布这期节目时，其中一些内容应该已经上线了。

sentences.en: Yeah, so, keep that in mind.
sentences.zh: 对，所以请记住这一点。

sentences.en: We also have partnerships.
sentences.zh: 我们也有合作伙伴关系。

sentences.en: So, we partnered with Headspace.
sentences.zh: 比如我们与 Headspace 进行了合作。

sentences.en: And I think this is an important partnership because it also extends the learning on emotional well-being.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一次重要的合作，因为它同样延伸了关于情感健康的学习。

sentences.en: And so, we have this wonderful podcast called Goodnight World.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们有了一档名为《晚安世界》（Goodnight World）的精彩播客。

sentences.en: We also partnered with Dr. Lori Santos on her Happiness Lab podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我们还与劳里·桑托斯博士（Dr. Lori Santos）在她的《幸福实验室》（Happiness Lab）播客上进行了合作。

sentences.en: And so, there are three episodes there.
sentences.zh: 那里有三期节目。

sentences.en: And there are other resources in terms of the books that we publish.
sentences.zh: 在我们出版的图书方面也有其他资源。

sentences.en: And we also, on our kid-facing, sesamestreet.org, there's lots of digital games and printables and storybooks that I think are also not only resources for mental health,
sentences.zh: 此外，在我们面向儿童的网站 sesamestreet.org 上，有许多数字游戏、可打印材料和故事书，我认为这些不仅是心理健康的资源，

sentences.en: but across that whole child curriculum.
sentences.zh: 而且贯穿了整个全人教育课程。

sentences.en: Our mission at Sesame Workshop is helping kids grow smarter.
sentences.zh: 我们在《芝麻街工作室》的使命是帮助孩子们更聪明地成长。

sentences.en: So, those are those processing skills plus the content skills stronger.
sentences.zh: $所以，这就是那些处理技能加上更强大的内容技能。

sentences.en: Those are the self-regulation and physical health and kinder.
sentences.zh: 这些就是自我调节、身体健康，还有更友善。

sentences.en: All right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: And we all need to be kinder in today's world.
sentences.zh: 我们在当今世界都需要更加友善。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Now, you've said in other interviews that young children's mental health is sometimes overlooked in discussions about the youth mental health crisis.
sentences.zh: 现在，你在其他采访中曾说过，在讨论青年心理健康危机时，幼儿的心理健康有时被忽视了。

sentences.en: Why do you think that is and why is it important to add that perspective to the conversation?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是为什么，为什么将这种视角引入讨论中如此重要？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that adults need some guidance in able to pick up on what is going on with their children.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为成年人在敏锐察觉孩子们身上发生了什么事情时需要一些指导。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 所以，

sentences.en: noticing how their children's big feelings might be interfering with their everyday life or there's regression in terms of regression in potty training or they may not be interested in eating their favorite foods anymore.
sentences.zh: 注意到孩子们那些强烈的情绪是如何干扰他们的日常生活，或者观察到他们在如厕训练上出现倒退，或者他们可能对再吃自己最喜欢的食物失去兴趣。

sentences.en: So, what are those signs or even other distress signs?
sentences.zh: 那么，这些迹象或其他痛苦信号是什么呢？

sentences.en: Because parents may not always realize that they could be struggling with some mental health issue.
sentences.zh: 因为父母可能并不总是意识到他们的孩子可能正在遭受某些心理健康问题的困扰。

sentences.en: And that's why we really wanted to get this next batch of content out about these feelings helpers.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们非常希望推出下一批关于这些“情绪助手”的内容。

sentences.en: That there are professionals who could help you.
sentences.zh: 即有专业人士可以帮助你。

sentences.en: And we need to destigmatize this idea that my child needs to see a therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 我们需要消除这种观念的污名化，即“我的孩子需要去看治疗师”。

sentences.en: A therapist is there to help, not to label, but to help you and the family work together to help the child with their resources to have a better understanding.
sentences.zh: 治疗师的存在是为了提供帮助，而不是为了贴标签，而是为了帮助你和家人共同努力，用资源帮助孩子更好地理解自我。

sentences.en: For instance, let's talk about anxiety.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们来谈谈焦虑。

sentences.en: So, children who are so anxious that they don't want to go to school or so anxious that they don't want to go to a friend's birthday party or they may not want to go to day camp.
sentences.zh: 有些孩子焦虑到不想去上学，或者焦虑到不想去参加朋友的生日派对，或者他们可能不想去日间夏令营。

sentences.en: I mean, this is an example of you want to be able to help your child so they're not missing out on these wonderful experiences.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个例子，说明你想能够帮助你的孩子，这样他们就不会错过这些美妙的经历。

sentences.en: But they may need some extra help and guidance.
sentences.zh: 但他们可能需要一些额外的帮助和指导。

sentences.en: So, what's the critical takeaway you want parents and other caregivers of young children to get from the materials that you're producing right now?
sentences.zh: 那么，你希望父母和幼儿的其他看护者从你目前制作的材料中得到的最关键的收获是什么？

sentences.en: Well, I want them to understand that there are a range of emotions and to give children the labels for these emotions.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我希望他们理解存在各种各样的情绪，并为孩子们提供这些情绪的标签。

sentences.en: To be able to distinguish.
sentences.zh: 能够加以区分。

sentences.en: It's not just happy, angry, sad, right?
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是快乐、生气、伤心，对吧？

sentences.en: There are other emotion words like disappointed and frustrated and jealous.
sentences.zh: 还有其他表示情绪的词，比如失望、沮丧和嫉妒。

sentences.en: That's an interesting one.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的词。

sentences.en: Jealous.
sentences.zh: 嫉妒。

sentences.en: What's jealous?
sentences.zh: 什么是嫉妒？

sentences.en: But to connect with your child.
sentences.zh: 但要与你的孩子建立联系。

sentences.en: So, observe these physical expressions of an emotion.
sentences.zh: 所以，观察这些情绪的身体表达。

sentences.en: Give the child a label.
sentences.zh: 给孩子贴上标签。

sentences.en: But validate.
sentences.zh: 但要认可。

sentences.en: Validate the emotion.
sentences.zh: 认可这种情绪。

sentences.en: I understand you are jealous because you are wanting something that your friend has.
sentences.zh: 我理解你感到嫉妒，因为你想要你朋友拥有的东西。

sentences.en: Jealous.
sentences.zh: 嫉妒。

sentences.en: What's jealous?
sentences.zh: 什么是嫉妒？

sentences.en: And so, now you have an opportunity to talk about the feeling.
sentences.zh: 所以，现在你有一个机会来谈论这种感觉。

sentences.en: Like, you think you're mad or angry, but you're really jealous.
sentences.zh: 比如，你觉得自己很生气或愤怒，但你其实是嫉妒。

sentences.en: But then come up with a strategy.
sentences.zh: 但随后要提出一个策略。

sentences.en: How do I be with this emotion?
sentences.zh: 我该如何与这种情绪相处？

sentences.en: Because all emotions are okay.
sentences.zh: 因为所有情绪都是正常的。

sentences.en: We all have these feelings.
sentences.zh: 我们都有这些感觉。

sentences.en: But how do I get beyond, I'm not going to talk to my friend Susie anymore because she's got the sparkly coat that I want.
sentences.zh: 但我该如何超越这一点，比如“我再也不和苏茜说话了，因为她有我想要的闪亮外套”？

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: So, what's a strategy?
sentences.zh: 那么，什么是策略呢？

sentences.en: And that's where these mindfulness strategies come in.
sentences.zh: 这就是这些正念策略发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: And that's where Sesame Workshop comes in because we're not there to tell the parents what you need to do.
sentences.zh: 这也是芝麻街工作室发挥作用的地方，因为我们不是来告诉父母你们需要做什么。

sentences.en: We're here to give them the language and the strategies to build our emotional well-being toolbox.
sentences.zh: 我们是来为他们提供语言和策略，来建立我们的情绪健康工具箱。

sentences.en: So, we're there for the how-to's.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们是为了提供具体方法而存在的。

sentences.en: I often get so upset when people say, oh, parents need to do this and they need to do that.
sentences.zh: 每当人们说，哦，父母需要这样做，他们需要那样做时，我经常感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: Well, show me how.
sentences.zh: 那么，做给我看。

sentences.en: Tell me how.
sentences.zh: 告诉我怎么做。

sentences.en: And that's where our videos and our resources come in.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的视频和资源发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: We're showing and telling how.
sentences.zh: 我们在展示和讲述具体方法。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Trulio, I want to thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 好的，特鲁利奥博士，我想感谢你今天加入我们。

sentences.en: And I also want to thank Sesame Workshop for collaborating with us.
sentences.zh: 我还想感谢芝麻街工作室与我们合作。

sentences.en: We have a great partnership and I know it's going to continue.
sentences.zh: 我们有着极好的合作关系，我知道它将继续下去。

sentences.en: And thank you for this partnership because we learned so much from all of your experts.
sentences.zh: 感谢这种合作关系，因为我们从你们所有的专家身上学到了很多。

sentences.en: So, and thank you, Kim, for having this wonderful chat today.
sentences.zh: 还有，谢谢你，金，今天进行了这次精彩的谈话。

sentences.en: I really enjoyed it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢。

sentences.en: It's been great.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: You can find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on our website at www.speakingofpsychology.org or on Apple, Spotify, YouTube, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 上，或者在 Apple、Spotify、YouTube 或你获取播客的任何地方找到《心理学聊天》之前的单集。

sentences.en: And if you like what you've heard, please subscribe and leave us a review.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢你所听到的内容，请订阅并给我们留下评价。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future podcasts, you can email us at speakingofpsychology at apa.org.
sentences.zh: 如果你对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，可以发电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology is produced by Lee Weinerman.
sentences.zh: 《心理学聊天》由李·维纳曼制作。

sentences.en: Our sound editor is Chris Kondayan.
sentences.zh: 我们的声音编辑是克里斯·孔达扬。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening to the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听美国心理学协会的节目。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。
